text: How does Rapid Spanning Tree achieve convergence in seconds rather than fifty?
choices: It recognises which ports connect to hosts rather than switches, and transitions those to forwarding immediately
It disables loop prevention on access ports
explanation: A port with a single host cannot create a loop, so the classic timers — set conservatively for 1980s network diameters — were guarding against a case that almost never arises in a modern access layer. Edge ports plus proposal/agreement handshaking do the rest.
